title: Prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels (BMC Chapter 13.63)
requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide a coordinated pricing algorithm to Berkeley landlords, and unlawful for a landlord to use one, to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley; each unit and each month of use is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue over either the sale or the use, and an aggrieved tenant may sue a landlord over its use, for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.

coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Applies to landlords and to anyone who sells or licenses such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
exemptions: The following are excluded from the definition of coordinated pricing algorithm: (a) products or processes that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or terms; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing guidelines; (c) products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance: Annual General Adjustment limit on rent increases (as amended by Measure BB)
requirement: Landlords of fully covered units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), which the Rent Board sets at 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase and which Measure BB caps at 5%. Banked (unused) AGAs may still raise rent above 5% up to the rent ceiling, and Regulation 1148 sets the eligibility and tenant-notice conditions for taking the increase.
key_value: AGA = 65% of Bay Area CPI-U increase, capped at 5%; 2026 AGA is 1.0% (65% of a 1.5% CPI increase), effective no earlier than 2026-01-01
coverage_conditions: Fully covered (rent ceiling and AGA limit apply): most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually under separate leases). Government-subsidized units (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME) fall within these categories where Federal or State law does not prohibit rent control. Utility charges for fully covered units must be included in base rent unless the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to hold the account.
exemptions: Not subject to rent control (partially covered, registration only): new construction with a Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums. Exempt: 'Golden Duplex' units (owner-occupied on Dec. 31, 1979, with an owner currently living in one unit); units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the owner, if the owner lived on the property at the start of the tenancy. Section 202, Section 811, and HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage projects with Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside or Project-based Section 8 subsidies are not rent-controlled. The 2026 AGA does not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
interaction: Government-subsidized units are fully covered by the rent ceiling only where Federal law, State law, or administrative regulation does not prohibit rent control.
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: Cartwright Act: ban on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute one while coercing another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California.
key_value: Unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (any methodology, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or influence a price or commercial term) (a) as part of a restraint-of-trade conspiracy, or (b) while coercing others to adopt its recommended price or commercial term
coverage_conditions: Applies to any person, other than the end consumer, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm for products or services in California. The law covers all industries and is not limited to rental housing, so it reaches residential rent-setting.
exemptions: Only algorithms used by two or more persons that use competitor data are covered. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data fall outside the definition. A secondary source notes that the statute does not expressly exempt non-confidential competitor data.
interaction: Nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
citation_full: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (added by Stats. 2025, ch. 338 (AB 325)); see also Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16756.1
penalty: Cartwright Act violations are punishable as a crime, per the Legislative Counsel's Digest; no specific penalty is stated in the bill text.

title: California Tenant Protection Act: just cause required to terminate tenancies
requirement: Once a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may terminate the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written termination notice. requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered residential tenancy without at-fault just cause (such as non-payment, material lease breach, nuisance or criminal activity) or good-faith no-fault just cause (owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government or court vacate order, or demolition or substantial remodel), and the termination notice must state the cause. title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirements
requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of the just causes listed in Section 37.9(a), and that cause must be the dominant motive; expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause. Evictions for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of a unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation also require relocation payments under Section 37.9C.
key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Section 37.9(a)
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits remain subject to the just cause eviction provisions. These include units whose first Certificate of Occupancy was issued after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
exemptions: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 rather than Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
penalty: Substantial civil and/or criminal liability for unlawful eviction or attempted eviction.
subject: landlord
supporting_spans: Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

corroborating_sources.quoted_span: The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation

plain_language.en: This rule lets San Francisco landlords evict covered tenants only for one of the 17 just causes in Section 37.9(a). Expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause. Some evictions also require relocation payments.
plain_language.es: Esta regla permite que los propietarios de San Francisco desalojen a inquilinos cubiertos solo por una de las 17 causas justas de la Sección 37.9(a). El vencimiento del contrato o un cambio de propietario no es causa justa. Algunos desalojos también requieren pagos de reubicación.

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance: annual allowable rent increase limits
requirement: For units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits, the annual allowable increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent (base rent × .016). The prior periods were 1.4% (3/1/2025–2/28/2026) and 1.7% (3/1/2024–2/28/2025).
key_value: 1.6% annual allowable increase for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027 (previously 1.4% for 3/1/2025–2/28/2026)
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, other than tenancies exempt from its rent increase limitations.
exemptions: Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act; some tenancies where the rent is regulated by another government agency. These tenancies remain subject to the Ordinance's just cause eviction provisions.
interaction: Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act (state law) makes some tenancies eligible for rent increases despite the Ordinance.
quoted_span: This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979
subject: landlord
supporting_spans: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance

corroborating_sources.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

plain_language.en: This rule limits annual rent increases for covered San Francisco units. From March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027, the allowed increase is 1.6% of base rent. Some tenancies are exempt from this limit.
plain_language.es: Esta regla limita los aumentos anuales de renta en unidades cubiertas de San Francisco. Del 1 de marzo de 2026 al 28 de febrero de 2027, el aumento permitido es 1.6% de la renta base. Algunos contratos están exentos de este límite.

title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
requirement: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects applicants and residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions. The source does not specify which screening practices are restricted or the required procedures.
coverage_conditions: Affordable housing decisions
quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
subject: landlord

plain_language.en: This ordinance protects applicants and residents with arrest or conviction history in San Francisco affordable housing decisions. The available source does not say which screening practices are restricted or what procedures are required.
